narr: For the end of June, a stretch of active weather occurred due to a cold front that rippled across Ohio and Pennsylvania and then sank into northern West Virginia while high pressure sprawled across the southeastern United States. A low pressure system pushed the front back to the north before pivoting east out of the Great Lakes region and dragging yet another front towards the middle Ohio Valley for he final few days of June. Each day, thunderstorms and heavy showers developed amid hot and humid conditions with most widespread activity generally occurring in the afternoon and evening hours. Activity then slowly diminished for the late night and early morning hours.||Soils were already primed for flooding by wet antecedent conditions from earlier in the month. Thus, these additional rounds of heavy rain were enough to instigate localized flooding across portions of the area late in the month. In West Virginia, flash flooding led to a few water rescues and mudslides, caused creeks to leave their banks, and impacted roads in Boone, Fayette, Kanawha, Lewis, Lincoln, Logan, Putnam, and Upshur Counties.

State Route 10 was closed near Chief Logan State Park due to flooding. Flooding was also observed in Henlawson, Mitchell Heights, and on the southbound lane of Route 44. Snap Branch Road and Hidden Valley Road were washed out from flooding. Mud and rock slides occurred along Route 10 near Henlawson and on Regency Heights Road.

High water was observed on Interstate 77 near milepost 77. A section of the Turnpike was also closed due to high water near mile marker 72. First Avenue in Montgomery experienced flooding. On US Route 60, flooding was observed between Diamond and Shrewsbury, and on the eastbound lanes under the Chelyan Bridge.

In Buckhannon, high water was observed on South Kanawha Street, South Florida Street, Madison Street, Vicksburg Road, East Main Street, and the intersection of Wood and Ritchie Streets. A water rescue occurred on Kelson Lane for an individual stuck upstairs due to flooding. Another rescue occurred on Vicksburg Road for a vehicle trapped in floodwaters.
High water was observed on Hackers Creek Road and other roadways in the area.
